About us

Our vision is independent and productive lives for the people we care for. We are a specialist healthcare provider that manufactures high technology medical devices including prosthetics and orthotics, for individual patients with an integrated rehabilitation, peer support, and coordination of care service.

    This redeveloped facility will help ensure people across the Northern region can access high-quality prosthetic and rehabilitation services in a modern, purpose-built environment, designed to support both clinical care and innovation.

    BLACK

    5,665 followers

    1mo

    BLACK was proud to deliver the refurbishment of 5-7 Horopito Street for Peke Waihanga, transforming an existing Mount Eden building into a purpose-built facility supporting New Zealand’s artificial limb services.   This complex technical refurbishment reconfigured an existing building to accommodate clinical, rehabilitation, administration and specialist production spaces. Works included a new two-storey timber-framed addition within a former internal courtyard, seismic strengthening, lift pit and core construction, foundation upgrades, partial re-roofing, and extensive building services integration.   A key challenge was excavating the new lift pit through near-solid basalt, with a large rock uncovered during the works retained as a feature at the building entrance.   Careful staging allowed critical workshop operations to continue throughout construction while new electrical, hydraulic, compressed air and specialist production services were integrated into the existing structure.   The completed facility improves accessibility, workflow and operational efficiency, while showcasing BLACK’s ability to deliver complex refurbishment and adaptive reuse projects alongside our high-end interior fitout portfolio.   Thank you to all the trades, consultants and suppliers who supported the successful delivery of this project.

    Wonderful to see cultural identity thoughtfully reflected in the final design. A meaningful outcome achieved through partnership, care and collaboration.

    Jason Visser
    1mo

    An incredible journey for a 16-year-old from Fiji who had been using the same prosthesis for approximately eight years. He presented with numerous challenges, as his previous prosthesis had ultimately failed to meet his needs. Despite this, he remains highly active in several sports and has limitless potential ahead of him. Following a successful check socket fitting, we progressed to his definitive prosthesis, thoughtfully incorporating elements of his Fijian heritage into the design. This outcome would not have been possible without the support and collaboration of the team at Peke Waihanga. The family is truly grateful for the care and commitment shown throughout the process. We look forward to continuing to support him every step of the way.

    Innovation in action! Last week, our clinicians trial-fitted a KAFO weighing just 900g for a patient living with MS - and the results were remarkable. Lightweight without compromising stability, it made a real difference to the patient’s comfort, control, and energy levels. At Peke Waihanga, we’re always learning, refining, and chasing better outcomes for the people we support. #Prosthetics #MS #KAFO #Innovation #PatientCare

    Sean Tickner
    4mo

    900 grams. That’s it. Last week we trial-fitted a KAFO weighing just 900g for a patient living with MS — and it was one of those moments that reminds you why we do this work. The fit, feel, and control were great, and the patient’s immediate response said everything. Lightweight without compromising stability is huge, especially when fatigue and energy conservation matters as much as alignment and safety. A big part of this success came down to the FIOR & GENTZ joints and the expert input from our Össur Australia and New Zealand supplier Anton Kemp whose depth of knowledge helped fine-tune the setup to the patient, not just the diagnosis. We’re always learning, refining and chasing better outcomes. Clinicians: what’s the lightest KAFO you’ve fitted recently, and what trade-offs did you have to manage? #Orthotics #KAFO #MultipleSclerosis #ClinicalOutcomes #AssistiveTechnology #RehabEngineering #ProstheticsAndOrthotics #PatientCentredCare #Teamwork
